title: Prompt-diff: cost forensics & variant compare pane
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design an interactive 'Prompt-diff' pane in Redwood Console that lets engineers and PMs compare two or more prompt/route variants side-by-side to understand token-level cost delta and attribution. The pane targets use cases where teams are optimizing prompt wording, truncation, system message placement, or switching model/quantization profiles and need immediate feedback on the cost implications and suggested pricing patterns to reduce unit economics. Deliverables: high-fidelity prototype for desktop Console, exportable comparison CSV/JSON, copy for help text, and a short motion spec for integration with Rollouts/A-B analysis.
background: Customers frequently ask: how much does this prompt tweak save at scale? Current Console views show aggregate cost and token histograms per route, but there is no quick way to compare prompt variants and attribute differences to system vs user tokens, prefix cache hits, or model variant changes. This ticket builds a focused forensic tool to reduce iteration time and prevent costly regressions in production prompts.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows side-by-side prompt input and rendered token breakdown (system/user/assistant/separators)
Per-variant token counts and token-type cost are computed using Console pricing rules and displayed with % delta
Ability to toggle attribution heuristics: 'message-level', 'utterance-split', and 'kv-cache-aware'
Export button produces a CSV with per-token-line items and a JSON export matching the Console API schema
Design sign-off from PM and two engineering reviewers and a short handoff doc for ENG runtime to implement attribution hooks
